tagline: Nineteen miles down the east shore of Seneca Lake.
intro: From Lodi Point State Marine Park the byway follows Route 414 south along the east side of Seneca Lake through the town of Hector, high on the side of the lake valley at first and lower as it goes. Near Watkins Glen, where Route 79 forks off up the hillside, it keeps to the foot of the valley close by the water, and it ends at Clute Park in Watkins Glen.
The lake beside it is 38 miles long and over 600 feet deep, deep enough for the Navy to test sonar in it. Underground springs keep the water moving and give it little chance to freeze.

moments.title: Lodi
moments.text: After 1828 steamboats made Lodi Point a regular stop, and its warehouses handled coal, lime, salt, lumber and grain until the trade had gone by 1905.

moments.title: Watkins Glen
moments.text: In 1948 the first Watkins Glen Grand Prix ran on the public streets of the village, the first road race held in the country after the war.

moments.title: Watkins Glen State Park
moments.text: Glen Creek has cut a gorge 400 feet deep here, and the Gorge Trail goes over, under and along its 19 waterfalls on stone bridges and more than 800 stone steps.
